Analytics only with explicit consent. Events reach the server no earlier than consent is given; refusal means the log stays on the device only, and the app works in full. Coordinates, names and user-entered text are never sent.

The app works without an account. It keeps an on-device local event log (which stories were opened, which routes were downloaded) and stores content downloads. The log contains no names and no free-form text and is tied to a random device identifier — this is pseudonymised, not anonymous, data. When the app is installed, the KUDY server issues the device a random identifier and a secret: the server keeps the identifier and a hash of the secret, the secret itself is stored only on the device and is sent to the KUDY server with every device request as the access key. To rate-limit requests, the server keeps a one-way hash of the IP address. Ratings of routes and places given in the app (a score and selected reasons, no free-form text) are also sent to the KUDY server and kept there together with the device identifier.

records.value: KUDY — audio guides for city walks. This page describes which data the project processes: the free web channel and the mobile app.

Location is used in the app during an active walk: background location runs while the walk is active and stops with it. The app does not send precise GPS coordinates to the KUDY server or record them in the event log. The online map loads tiles from OpenFreeMap; tile requests reveal the viewed map area to that provider, including the area around your current position while map following is on. The web channel does not detect the visitor’s position.

review.note: Map tile requests disclose the viewed area to OpenFreeMap; precise GPS coordinates are not sent to the KUDY server or event log.

records.value: Purchases go through the app stores (App Store, Google Play): payment data is handled by the store, and the app records only the purchase event fact — route, variant, outcome — with no banking details. Entitlements are managed by a separate service, RevenueCat: the app sends it the random device identifier as the buyer identifier and the requests to purchase or to confirm earlier purchases; payments themselves go only through the store. The KUDY server keeps a technical record of purchase events (product, store, validity term) with no payment details.
